title: DataObject
description: A passive application element: data that application components, functions and services create, read, transform or pass along, modelled as the thing held rather than as the declaration of its shape. In code it is a domain object: a class or object that holds state and keeps that state consistent, with methods that only validate, derive from or change its own fields and no injected dependencies, whether it is declared as a class or built as an object by a factory function or a literal (a value object such as Money or DateRange, an aggregate held in memory such as a basket or a draft order, a client-side store, a context value); or it is data handled with no declared shape of its own (an untyped object, map or parsed JSON value). Use data-model ObjectSchema instead when the symbol only declares a shape: an interface, object type alias, record, struct or dataclass of named, typed fields with at most generated or trivial accessors and constructors, or an interface or type that declares the state of a store or context value beside the callbacks over that state, whether or not its shape is persisted or published, or the class is a persisted entity or ORM model; the object schema may realize the data object, and that relationship is what tells data held to a declared shape from data that is not. Use ApplicationComponent instead when the class or object encapsulates substantive behavior or dependencies (injected collaborators, business logic, I/O) and acts as a modular, replaceable unit rather than as a carrier of state. Use ApplicationEvent instead when the structure represents the occurrence of a state change that is published or dispatched to trigger reactive behavior, rather than data that is merely accessed; a record named for an occurrence (an OrderPlaced, an ...IntegrationEvent) that is published to a bus or dispatched to handlers is an event even when it holds only fields. Use ApplicationInterface instead when the type is an access point (an endpoint binding, controller or client stub) through which a service is invoked, rather than the data exchanged through it; a language-level interface that declares a service's operations is an ApplicationService.

documentation.description: Free-text description of what information the data object holds, its main fields and which components produce or consume it; set it whenever the symbol name alone does not convey the data's meaning.

x-dr-evidence: A class with fields and methods that act only on those fields (validate(), total(), addItem(), withStatus()), no injected dependencies and no ORM mapping, such as a value object or an aggregate held in memory.

Instances are constructed, mapped and mutated by other classes, while the class itself is more than a declaration of fields and carries no ORM table mapping, OpenAPI schema annotation or UI binding that would place it in a more specific layer.
A parameter, field or return value typed as any, object, dict or Map<string, unknown>, or a parsed JSON value, passed between functions with no interface, type or schema declaring its fields.

An object built by a store factory or as a literal, with no class declaration, that holds state fields beside the functions that set, toggle, reset or select that state (the result of a create(...) or defineStore(...) call, the value given to a UI context provider); the interface or type that declares its shape is an ObjectSchema that realizes it.
